[1] He is known especially for his historical works on Dauphiné, as well as his erotic dialogue called "The School of Women, or The Seven Flirtatious Encounters of Aloisia" (French: "L'Academie des dames, ou les Sept entretiens galants d'Aloisia" ).
[2] In the former dialogue, he posits a mathematical theorem now known as the Spiral of Theodorus.
[3] In geometry, the spiral of Theodorus (also called "square root spiral", "Einstein spiral" or "Pythagorean spiral") is a spiral composed of contiguous right triangles.
[4] The Statesman (Greek: Πολιτικός , "Politikos"; Latin: "Politicus"), also known by its Latin title, Politicus, is a Socratic dialogue written by Plato.
